newsitem.title: UK: Brazil, Mexico eye dollar bonds after Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, Mexico eye dollar bonds after Argentina.

text.p: Brazil and Mexico were considering launching dollar bonds following stronger-than-expected demand for Argentina's jumbo deal, traders said on Wednesday.
"After the over-subscription of Argentina, other major Latin American borrowers will be tempted to launch longer-dated dollar deals," said a syndicate official at a European bank.
On Tuesday, Argentina launched a $2.0 billion 20-year global bond, which will be priced later to yield 462.5 basis points over U.S. Treasury bonds, lower than the 475 b.p. spread talk.
Spreads on other Latin American bonds tightened by around 10 b.p. in anticipation of the bond performing well, dealers said.
Traders said Brazil was eyeing a $1.0 billion 10-year bond and Mexico could also launch a $1.0 billion transaction.

"Brazil is expected to do something soon, but we really do not know what shape it will take," said a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank. "They tend to go for the cheapest funding option. Demand is definitely there for a 10-year issue."
Mexico was unlikely to increase a $1.0 billion 10-year global bond launched on January 9, dealers said. Launched at a 335 b.p. spread, the deal has tightened to 302 b.p.
A longer-dated transaction was considered more likely for Mexico, dealers said. There has been talk it might issue another global bond to buy back Brady debt like it did last year.
Already scheduled is a 500 billion lire 10-year bond for Mexico due in the next few weeks via Chase.
